issues: Covers slightly lower, spend per head up 30p in a slow pre Christmas shopping period.
Delivery additionals 1,300 GBP with zero inaccurate orders; prep time up a minute. Extra tablets coming from London to streamline multi platform delivery tracking.
Labour slightly over target on staff training hours in Glasgow; food variance 3.3%.
Curran and Cameron have holidays coming up; kitchen supervisor recruitment picked up after Hanna boosted the job posts; cleaner interviews this week.
Compliance 99%; bar floor sprayed for bar flies (48 hours before mopping); vent certificates and an Anel service scheduled; fire panel serviced by Peter Brown.
Region: food spend target temporarily raised to 26% until current promotions end (Matthew Jenner).
Region: hats or hairnets mandatory for all staff to prevent food contamination.
Region: menu to be redesigned with spice levels built into all ramen dishes and free chillies removed.
Region: GM and HC meeting notes must run through Google Meet so Gemini takes the notes; budget router templates updated, Monday dates must be entered correctly.
Sales were £51,916.98, down £1,922.88 (3.57%) week on week and £8,720.52 (14.38%) below the £60,637.50 target, the third week running below target.
The GM expects trade to pick up from the 26th, and Howard described it as the usual quiet pre Christmas period, expecting a pick up from mid November.
Labour was 22.71% because of staff training, and the GM/HC meeting asked for labour to be cut or breaks extended during quieter periods.
Food cost was 23.41%, up from 21.80% last week.
Food usage variance was -4.7% and wet usage variance 3.7%, giving -3.3% overall.
Deliveroo had 0% rejected, cancelled and late orders and no refunds, and the GM queried whether moving off the Deliveroo tablet will affect prep time.
The site received twenty two 5 star and two 4 star reviews (12 at 4.92 stars on the BOH report, none at 3 stars or below).
BOH compliance has improved because all staff now know the process, but BOH closing cleanliness must be brought up to standard before leaving.
Penny saw a stock value above £10,000 in the stock count; Howard uses his own par levels, set after weekend run outs of chicken, ramen and tonkotsu, and says orders were wild when he took over.
The sushi section is improving with no more 20 minute waits.

Howard is hiring a chef (one trained yesterday and was good) but still has no supervisor because chefs are reluctant to take charge, and Penny suggested Dana, who already knows opening and closing compliance.
The fire panel still needs maintenance, and the site is waiting for the fire system manufacturer to attend.
The App, XOXO, Slerp and the lunch menu are the upcoming promotions, and the team has been informed about the change in protein and broth.

Region: five of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites ran food cost above 25% (Maki 12, 1, 7, 3 and 8), which the Scotland BOH meeting of 13/10 linked to loyalty programme and delivery platform discounts across the group.

Region: new tonkotsu and chicken broth arrives from 15/10 and needs no added water; defrost it a day ahead and reheat it in a pot rather than straight on the heat, and a digital Brix meter is arriving to replace checking by eye, though not every site has one yet (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: new chicken arrives on 15/10 and the new char siu (different shape) and pre cooked frozen beef from 19/10, starting at Maki 8; defrost the beef a day ahead and grill or pan fry it for 15 seconds a side before slicing, holding extra stock because it cannot be used on the day it arrives (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: the frozen ramen promotion is postponed by one week, and Penny is checking with Michael whether frozen ramen counts in food cost or separately, as some sites have already bought it (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).
